title: Review a cross-border personal data transfer
summary: Before allowing a new international data flow or materially changing a receiving supplier. A documented transfer decision with applicable safeguards, contracts and technical controls verified.
outcomes: A documented transfer decision with applicable safeguards, contracts and technical controls verified.
guidance: Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.
when: Before allowing a new international data flow or materially changing a receiving supplier.

parts.title: Map the actual transfer and access paths
parts.guidance: Identify the exporter, importer, data, purpose, storage locations and remote-access locations. Include onward transfers and supplier support access rather than relying only on the cloud region label.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: Prepare or reconcile the specified private evidence and documents; external changes and decisions use their own approved steps.

parts.title: Determine the applicable transfer requirements
parts.guidance: Qualified privacy advisers assess the relevant jurisdictions, roles and available transfer mechanisms. Record the basis and conditions for the specific flow, including unresolved local-law or supplier questions.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: The accountable person performs the decision, expert assessment or personal interaction described in this step. Supporting preparation does not authorize that act.

parts.title: Prepare the contract and risk evidence
parts.guidance: Assemble the proposed terms, supplier disclosures, security measures and any required assessment. Describe technical controls and alternatives without assuming a signed template alone resolves the risks.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: Prepare or reconcile the specified private evidence and documents; external changes and decisions use their own approved steps.

parts.title: Approve and implement the defined transfer
parts.guidance: Authorized owners execute reviewed agreements and configure the approved access and security measures. Keep unapproved destinations and onward transfers blocked and retain the decision evidence.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: The accountable person performs the decision, expert assessment or personal interaction described in this step. Supporting preparation does not authorize that act.

parts.title: Monitor supplier and legal changes
parts.guidance: Review changes in subprocessors, locations, purposes or safeguards and track contract obligations. Reassess the transfer when its documented assumptions change and suspend flows where required conditions are no longer met.

notes.text: This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.
Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.
